## What The Business Is

Oracle Corp. is a global enterprise technology company centered on databases, cloud infrastructure, enterprise applications, and industry software. It is now led by co-CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia, with Safra Catz having moved to executive vice chair in September 2025. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2025/Oracle-Corporation-Announces-Promotion-of-Clay-Magouyrk-and-Mike-Sicilia-to-CEOs-Safra-Catz-Appointed-Executive-Vice-Chair-of-the-Board-of-Directors/default.aspx?utm_source=openai)) Oracle’s current strategic identity is increasingly “full stack”: OCI cloud infrastructure for AI and enterprise workloads, Oracle Database and related data services, and SaaS applications such as Fusion ERP/HCM/SCM/CX, NetSuite, and Oracle Health.

## What It Does

Oracle sells cloud and license support, cloud infrastructure, database services, enterprise applications, hardware, and services. OCI competes with hyperscale clouds while emphasizing high-performance networking, database-native workloads, sovereign/dedicated regions, and large AI clusters. Oracle also embeds AI into applications: in the Q4 FY2026 transcript, management said it had delivered more than 1,000 AI agents across application suites and is testing token and outcome-based pricing for more advanced agentic use cases. Recent product news included Fusion Agentic Applications for CX and a builder in Oracle AI Agent Studio for connecting Oracle, partner, and external agents. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/oracle-introduces-fusion-agentic-applications-for-customer-experience-302737686.html?utm_source=openai)) Oracle also continues to push multicloud database access through offerings with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud; in April, Oracle and AWS announced plans to expand private multicloud networking between OCI and AWS. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/oracle-and-aws-collaborate-to-expand-multicloud-networking-302743862.html?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Oracle’s June 10 FY2026 results showed accelerating cloud demand: Q4 revenue was $19.2 billion, up 21% year over year, cloud infrastructure revenue rose 93%, cloud applications revenue rose 10%, and remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363%. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Record-Q4-and-FY-2026-Results-Driven-by-Cloud-Infrastructure--Cloud-Applications/?utm_source=openai)) Management said full-year FY2026 revenue exceeded $67 billion, non-GAAP operating income was $29 billion, and operating cash flow rose 54% to $32 billion; it also guided FY2027 total revenue growth of about 34% in constant currency, with cloud revenue expected to grow 58%–64% in Q1 FY2027. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Record-Q4-and-FY-2026-Results-Driven-by-Cloud-Infrastructure--Cloud-Applications/?utm_source=openai))  

AI infrastructure momentum was the key narrative in the transcript: management said Oracle signed $67 billion of AI infrastructure contracts in Q4, had 97.5% global GPU utilization, and delivered more than 1.2 gigawatts of capacity to customers in FY2026. Oracle also highlighted large sites in Texas, New Mexico, Michigan, and Wisconsin, plus FY2027 Q1 delivery approaching 1 gigawatt. Separately, Bloom Energy announced an expanded strategic partnership to deploy up to 2.8 GW to support Oracle’s AI and cloud infrastructure buildout. ([nasdaq.com](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/bloom-energy-and-oracle-expand-strategic-partnership-deploy-28-gw-accelerate-ai?utm_source=openai))  

Oracle Health also showed deployment progress: VA reported the federal EHR went live at four more medical centers in Southern Ohio/Kentucky on June 6, following four Michigan deployments earlier in 2026. ([news.va.gov](https://news.va.gov/147501/vas-federal-ehr-rollout-success-continues-in-southern-ohio/?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

The same AI buildout is pressuring cash flow, margins, and the balance sheet. Oracle said FY2026 net cash outlay for capex was $48 billion and guided FY2027 net capex outlay to around $70 billion, supported by customer prepayments but also requiring about $40 billion of debt and equity, including a $20 billion at-the-market equity issuance. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Record-Q4-and-FY-2026-Results-Driven-by-Cloud-Infrastructure--Cloud-Applications/?utm_source=openai)) The Register noted that despite strong Q4 revenue, Oracle’s shares fell as investors focused on data-center capex and funding needs. ([theregister.com](https://www.theregister.com/paas-and-iaas/2026/06/11/oracles-ai-datacenter-splurge-gives-investors-the-capex-jitters/5254035?utm_source=openai))  

Gross margin is also under near-term pressure from OCI/data-center mix and ramp timing; management said FY2026 gross margin stepped down about five points and expects another FY2027 step-down before infrastructure margins improve as contracted capacity converts to revenue. Execution risk is high because the AI backlog depends on timely delivery of power, GPUs, networking, construction, and customer workloads. Prior reporting also pointed to delays at some Oracle/OpenAI data-center projects due to tight materials and skilled-labor supply, underscoring supply-chain and buildout risk even if demand remains intact. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/oracle-reportedly-delays-several-new-openai-data-centers-because-of-shortages-tight-material-and-labor-supply-frustrate-expansion-plans-possibly-by-a-year-or-more?utm_source=openai))  

Oracle Health remains a reputational and operational watch item. While VA rollouts resumed, Federal News Network cited prior GAO findings that only 13% of surveyed VA staff using the Oracle-Cerner EHR believed it made VA as efficient as possible, and 58% believed it increased patient-safety risks. ([federalnewsnetwork.com](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/it-modernization/2026/06/va-ehr-rollout-continues-with-4-more-deployments/?utm_source=openai))
